body:
Why an AI strategy matters now

AI tools are cheap to try and easy to buy, so most businesses end up with scattered experiments: a few ChatGPT accounts, an AI feature switched on in one system, a pilot that never moved past the demo. Spending drifts, risks go unmanaged, and nobody can say what the business has gained. An AI strategy brings order. It identifies the handful of initiatives that will genuinely move revenue, cost or customer experience, puts them in a sensible order and assigns accountability.

A strategy is also what boards, investors and large clients increasingly ask to see. They want to know how you use AI, how you control it and how it supports the plan for the business.

What our AI strategy engagement covers

  1. Goals and constraints. We start with your business plan, not the technology: growth targets, margin pressure, capacity limits and customer expectations.
  2. Opportunity discovery. Workshops with leaders and the people doing the work uncover where time, errors and lost revenue sit today.
  3. Scoring. Each opportunity is rated on value, effort, data readiness and risk, so the ranking is transparent and defensible.
  4. Build, buy or wait. For each initiative we recommend whether to use an existing tool, build something custom or hold off.
  5. Roadmap. A 90-day plan with quick wins first, owners, milestones, budgets in AUD and success measures, plus a view of the following six to twelve months.
  6. Governance. Accountability, an AI usage policy, a register of AI systems and review points.

How we prioritise AI initiatives

QuadrantValueEffort and riskWhat we recommend
Quick winsHighLowStart in the first 30 days
Strategic betsHighHighPlan carefully, pilot, then scale
Nice to haveLowLowBundle with other work or leave to staff tools
Avoid for nowLowHighRevisit when tools or data mature

Quick wins matter. A first project that saves hours within weeks builds trust with staff and frees budget for the bigger bets.

Governance built on Australian guidance

Our strategies follow the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption, which sets out six essential practices: decide who is accountable, understand impacts and plan accordingly, measure and manage risks, share essential information, test and monitor, and maintain human control. We also map initiatives against Australia’s AI Ethics Principles and the OAIC’s privacy guidance for AI products.

In practice, governance is right-sized: a small business gets a one-page policy and a simple register, while a larger organisation gets defined roles, risk assessments and review cycles.

What you receive

  • An executive summary for the board or owners
  • The scored opportunity register
  • The 90-day roadmap with budgets in AUD
  • Business cases for the top initiatives
  • An AI usage policy and AI system register
  • A presentation and Q&A session with your leadership team

Who AI strategy consulting suits

It suits Australian SMEs and mid-sized organisations with more than one possible AI use case, a leadership team that needs a shared plan, or pressure from customers or a board to show progress. If you already know the single task you want to automate, you may not need a full strategy. A focused AI Readiness Assessment or a direct build through AI automation may be quicker.

How the engagement runs

  1. Free AI audit to confirm scope and who should be involved.
  2. Discovery through workshops and interviews, on site in Melbourne or by video.
  3. Analysis of opportunities, data, systems and risks.
  4. Roadmap workshop with your leadership team to agree priorities.
  5. Handover of all documents, with the option for our team to deliver the first initiatives.

Smaller businesses usually complete the process in two to three weeks; multi-department organisations in four to six. Read more about our wider AI consulting services.

Common mistakes an AI strategy avoids

Without a plan, businesses tend to buy tools before defining the problem, run pilots with no success measure, let staff paste client data into public chatbots, and spread a small budget across too many experiments. A good strategy prevents each of these by setting clear goals, one owner per initiative, a usage policy and a short list of priorities. It also gives you permission to say no to the AI pitches that don’t fit.
faqs: How long does an AI strategy take to build?
For most SMEs, two to three weeks from kick-off to roadmap. Organisations with several departments or complex systems usually take four to six weeks.
Do we need technical staff to create an AI strategy?
No. We bring the technical expertise. We need time from the people who run and do the work, plus access to someone who knows your systems.
What does an AI roadmap include?

A prioritised list of AI initiatives with owners, milestones, budgets in AUD, success measures and risks for the next 90 days, plus a view of the following six to twelve months and the governance to manage it.
Will you build the initiatives in the roadmap?
If you want us to. Because we also deliver automation, agents and custom AI, the roadmap is realistic. You can also hand it to your own team or another provider.
